clue.text: More than is required for six deliveries?

definitions.text: More than is required for six deliveries?

parts.words: More than is required for six deliveries?
parts.note: in cricket six deliveries make an over, so the clue reads as the room for one set of six balls, while its plain sense is surplus ability to produce

explanation.surface: A remark about having more room than a cricket over of six balls needs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled in a row; the question mark flags that the clue is a pun on that word plus room or ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcapacity is an excess of productive ability beyond what demand calls for.

clue.text: The rebuilt AA motel's popular in Scotland

definitions.text: The rebuilt AA motel's popular in Scotland

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A roadside motel run by the Automobile Association has been refurbished and is a hit north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of AA MOTEL ('rebuilt') gives the answer; the whole clue also describes porridge oats, a staple Scots food.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal, ground oats used for porridge and oatcakes, is a traditional staple of the Scottish diet.

clue.text: People in TV without vision coming up for oxygen, say

indicators.note: in signals that one piece goes inside another
in a down entry, coming up means the letters read from bottom to top
without signals that the following word is taken away from the longer one

parts.note: TV is short for television
taken as written
men means people in the general sense

explanation.surface: Viewers who lose the picture on their set come up for air.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'coming up' reads the stripped word from the bottom, before the people go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxygen is one example of a chemical element, signalled by 'say'.

clue.text: To which "plant" can allude, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A riddle about which flower the word plant might hint at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' marks CAN ALLUDE as an anagram; 'To which' just introduces the riddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Calendula, the pot marigold, is a flowering garden plant.

clue.text: Crash is a pain? About right

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a pang is a sudden sharp pain

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if a car crash is a nuisance and decides that is about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts PANG around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Prang is British slang for a crash, especially a minor car accident.

clue.text: A sort of cover where foreign vehicles enter …

definitions.text: A sort of cover where foreign vehicles enter …

parts.words: A sort of cover where foreign vehicles enter …
parts.note: read as a harbour through which imported motors come into the country, though the plain sense is a roofed shelter for parking a motor

explanation.surface: Describes a shelter at a harbour where imported cars arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue, which is also a car cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A carport is an open-sided roofed shelter for parking a vehicle.

clue.text: … or is this the appropriate cover?

definitions.text: … or is this the appropriate cover?

parts.words: … or is this the appropriate cover?
parts.note: continuing the previous clue's car covers, this asks about another kind: a fitted cover over an open vehicle's rear seats or load bed

explanation.surface: Asks whether a different car cover would suit better.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonneau is the rear passenger area of an open car, and a tonneau cover is fitted over it.

clue.text: Senior linesman?

parts.note: a linesman is usually a match official, but here it is someone who writes lines of verse, and the senior one holds a national post

explanation.surface: Sounds like the most experienced assistant referee at a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Linesman' wants to be a football or tennis official; the lines are poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Poet Laureate is the officially appointed national poet, the most senior writer of verse lines.

clue.text: Betrayal on switching parts to do well as trader

indicators.note: switching parts means the two halves of the word change places

parts.note: a sellout is a betrayal of principles or allies

explanation.surface: Treachery that pays off for a merchant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching parts' swaps the two halves SELL and OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsell is to sell more than a rival, a trader's form of success.

clue.text: A doctor with elan, perhaps, describing a gland

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters may be ordered differently

explanation.surface: A physician with flair is giving a description of a gland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ELAN to ENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenal is the adjective for the glands above the kidneys, so it describes a gland.

clue.text: Doubtful railway supporter easily brought round?

parts.note: light in the sense of flimsy or lacking weight, so not to be relied on
a sleeper is a beam that supports railway track

explanation.surface: A flimsy track beam that is easy to win over.
explanation.walkthrough: A sleeper is the British name for a railway tie, the beam under the rails.
explanation.definitionFit: A light sleeper is a person who wakes easily, that is, is roused without effort.

clue.text: The other side's said to be batting in that place

indicators.note: said means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: their means belonging to the other side
in cricket the side batting is said to be in

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator notes the opposition is now at the crease over there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' turns THEIR into its sound-alike THERE; IN is cricket's term for the side batting.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein is a formal word meaning within that place or thing.

clue.text: Popular person anticipated for breakfast?

definitions.meaning: an informal phrase for a decent, likeable individual
read literally, a fine boiled or fried egg is something hoped for at the morning meal

explanation.definitionFit: Good egg is old-fashioned slang for a pleasant, reliable person, and literally a tasty egg.

clue.text: Leader abstaining in vote for grant

indicators.note: the leader abstaining means the first letter of the word drops out

parts.note: a ballot is a vote

explanation.surface: A party leader sits out the vote on a funding grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader abstaining' removes B, the first letter of BALLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to grant or assign a share to someone.

clue.text: One to expect confidently to be an investment

parts.note: a unit is one single thing
to trust is to hope or expect with confidence

explanation.surface: Someone sure that a single item will be a sound investment.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit trust is a pooled investment fund in which investors buy units.

clue.text: Twisting irons into a plant shape

indicators.note: twisting means the letters are wrung into a new order

explanation.surface: Bending metal bars into the form of a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisting' rearranges IRONS INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Intorsion is the spiral twisting of a plant stem, a botanical term for its shape.

clue.text: The rambling society natter is unyielding

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A walking club's chatter refuses to give way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' suggests a walking club, but it rearranges S with NATTER IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistant means opposing or withstanding something, so not yielding.

clue.text: Take in regulations set up at base

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means the word is written upwards

parts.note: laws are regulations
low means base or mean

explanation.surface: Rules laid down at the bottom must be absorbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns LAWS to SWAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow is to take in, whether food or a story.

clue.text: Cutter changing places on lake

indicators.note: changing means the letters alter their order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A woodcutter moves house to a spot by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges PLACES to SCALPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalpel is a surgeon's small sharp knife, a cutting tool.

clue.text: Smooth to and fro

indicators.note: to and fro means it reads the same in both directions

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Sanding something flat by moving back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to and fro' says the answer reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: To level is to make smooth and flat; level is also an adjective for even.

clue.text: Voting decisively without power, taking all things together

indicators.note: without means the letter is dropped

parts.note: plumping means choosing firmly, as in plumping for a candidate

explanation.surface: A firm vote cast without strength, counting everything as one.
explanation.walkthrough: To plump for something is to choose it decisively; 'without' removes P.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumping means grouping things together, as in lumping them all in one category.

clue.text: Exceptionally, rain gets into tank: not normal

indicators.note: gets into means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a vat is a large tank

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Rare rainfall ends up in a storage tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant is a form that differs from the standard, so not normal.

clue.text: Note chap in reserves returning determined

parts.note: Adam, the first man, stands for a chap

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside another
returning means the word reads backwards

parts.note: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: A soldier in the reserves comes home resolute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns TA to AT; 'in' puts N inside it. The TA was Britain's volunteer reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means firmly decided and refusing to be swayed.

clue.text: Sentimental time for bird sound

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: sweet means sentimental, as in a sweet story

explanation.surface: A tender moment marked by birdsong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps T in place of the S of SWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is the chirp of a small bird.

clue.text: Pity about the small piece left off

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: off means the letter is removed

parts.note: a morsel is a small piece of food

explanation.surface: Sorry that a little bit was left off the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' takes L away from MORSEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Pity can mean regret or sorrow over a wrong, which is remorse.

clue.text: Pieces of film in middle of reel showing darkening

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another
middle of means the central letters of the word are taken

parts.note: clips are short extracts of film

explanation.surface: Film extracts on a spool showing a fading picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclipse is the darkening of the sun or moon when another body blocks its light.

clue.text: Scruffy mite grasps the alphabet to make impression

indicators.note: grasps means one piece holds another inside it
scruffy means untidy, so the letters are messed about

parts.note: ITA is the Initial Teaching Alphabet, a reading scheme used in British schools

explanation.surface: An untidy little creature gets hold of the ABC to make an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: The Initial Teaching Alphabet was a phonetic alphabet once used to teach British children to read.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate someone is to do an impression of them.

clue.text: Play time?

definitions.meaning: the evening ending the Christmas festivities, on 5 or 6 January

explanation.definitionFit: Twelfth Night is both a Shakespeare comedy and the eve of Epiphany, a date in the calendar.
